text:
monitoring-bot: [ALERT] region=us-west1 severity=critical -> 60m spike in 5xx from inference endpoints, host-level heartbeats failing, affected hosts: gpu-pool-*-uswest1 :rotating_light:

jordan_sre: seeing same in our dashboards. CI-slo graphs showing latency/timeouts. can oncall confirm network/host reachability?

ashley_infra: I can't ssh to the gateway instances in us-west1 from our jumpbox. `ssh` hangs. provider console shows many hosts UNREACHABLE.

matt_ops: paging oncall, marking this P1. opening incident tracker: https://incidents.internal.redwood/INC-2024-311 (created). @jordan_sre you're incident commander unless you assign.

jordan_sre: taking it. oncall: @ashley_infra @matt_ops please list immediate mitigations.

ashley_infra: steps I'm starting:
- `gcloud compute instances list --filter="zone:(us-west1*) AND status!=RUNNING"` to enumerate
- check provider status: https://status.cloudprovider.example.com/ -> reports "Network disruption in us-west1"
- scaling policy isn't kicking for autoscale because control plane API timeouts observed
trying to reroute control traffic to us-west2.

tilly_cs: support is getting multiple customer reports about timeouts for inference calls. I'll prepare a status notice draft for customers once we have failover plan.

jordan_sre: quick triage: looks like a full region network outage (BGP/edge?) not just GPU driver. Can we shift traffic to us-west2/us-east1? Does traffic-shifter support region-based failover?

ashley_infra: traffic-shifter can do weighted routing per region. I'll start a manual redirect for inference-prod to prefer us-west2 at 100% for new sessions. Note: sessions with warm KV cache will degrade. Command: `traffic-shifter promote --service=inference-prod --to-region=us-west2 --mode=immediate --note="failover us-west1 outage"`

deploy-bot: scheduled job created: failover-job-1715000200 -> executing traffic-shifter promote (dry-run flagged OFF).

jordan_sre: wait on full promote; we should do a canary for 5% then ramp to 100% to avoid overloading us-west2. Also check reserved GPU capacity in us-west2.

ashley_infra: good call. checking reserved pools: us-west2 has 40% free reserved GPUs (dedicated), but shared pools are near 80% used. I can route 10% first: `traffic-shifter promote --pct=10`

devops-bot: `kubectl -n inference get pods --selector=component=worker -o wide` -> us-west2 has 120 healthy pods, avg CPU 70%, queue backlog visible.

jordan_sre: start 10% shift now. Meanwhile, any indication of control plane/event stream loss? Are instance metadata or autoscaler healthy?

ashley_infra: control plane API to provider is intermittent. Autoscaler API calls are timing out; I triggered a manual scale-up for a backup pool in us-west2: `scale-backup-pool --region=us-west2 --count=50` (requested). Provider accepted the request but action pending due to quota checks.

matt_ops: I'm notifying sales and execs with a short summary, ETA unknown. severity=P1. Postmortem owner: @ashley_infra.

tilly_cs: customer status draft: "We are investigating a partial outage affecting inference in us-west1. Traffic is being shifted to alternate regions. Some requests may see increased latency. We will post updates every 15 minutes." Approving?
jordan_sre: send that, include link to incident tracker and recommended mitigations for affected customers (retry/backoff).

monitoring-bot: [AUTOMATION] created alert channel #incidents-us-west1 for on-call coordination.

ashley_infra: 10% shift live. Observability: error rate in us-west1 continues to climb (likely progressive failure). us-west2 error rate increased slightly but within acceptable SLOs.

jordan_sre: good. plan: 10% -> 50% in 3 min -> 100% in 8 min if metrics stable. also we need to open support ticket with cloud provider. ashley, can you escalate to provider L2?

ashley_infra: escalated via provider console, case #CP-98761, contact on call assigned. provider suggests they see "edge network instability". asked for ETA, they said investigating.

matt_ops: cost note: shifting to other regions will increase egress and peak GPU usage; I'm opening a temporary budget watch and alerting finance.

devops-bot: Canary metrics after 5m: us-west2 latency +12%, error rate +0.7%, request throughput stable. Queue backlog reduced in us-west1 gradually.

jordan_sre: ramp to 50% now. Keep monitoring: token-level cost impact, per-route latencies, and any cold-start spikes.

ashley_infra: 50% shift done. Some long-lived sessions in us-west1 are dropping; we will allow session reconnects to pick new region. Triggering KV-cache warmup jobs in us-west2 to reduce regen penalty.

tilly_cs: posted update to customers, sending direct pings to top 10 accounts.

matt_ops: provider gave initial ETA >2 hours. Need contingency if provider can't restore: consider moving some workloads to dedicated capacity in us-east1 or enabling pre-provisioned spare pools. Action item: @ashley_infra create runbook for cross-region emergency migration and estimate lead time.

jordan_sre: agreed. for now keep rolling to 100% gradually. If error rates exceed thresholds in destination region, pause and revert to hybrid mode.

monitoring-bot: New alert: control-plane API error rate -> 30% in us-west1, tagging incident.

ashley_infra: starting drafting postmortem notes into the incident doc (INC-2024-311). I'll include timeline, mitigation steps, and follow-ups: reserved pool sizing, cross-region traffic-shift rehearsals, early detection rule for BGP/edge errors.

jordan_sre: summary of immediate next steps:
- complete ramp to 100% if destination metrics hold (jordan)
- provider escalation and ETA tracking (ashley)
- customer comms every 15m (tilly)
- cost/watch alert (matt)
- incident doc and postmortem owner (ashley)
ashley_infra: 100% traffic shift completed at last step. us-west1 remains largely degraded and hosts are reported unreachable. keeping channel open for updates.

matt_ops: logging P1 closure conditions: provider restores region OR sustained degraded no longer impacting customers and jobs rebalanced.

jordan_sre: incident remains active. next update in 15m unless things change. thanks all. :handshake:
